root_idea.summary: The root centers on weakness or diminished vigor, especially as languor, slackness, or remissness.
root_idea.development: The semantic range develops from weakness to fatigue and languor, then to slackening or falling short in an action or affair; related nominal usage describes languid deportment.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied QAC group is a Quran-attested Form I verb with an independently supported lexical use.

senses.definition: To undertake or continue an action languidly; to slacken in it.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb is a dual imperfect in a prohibition concerning an ongoing activity, expressing failure to persist in it with vigor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass from, leave, or desist from a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested with عَنْهُ, in contrast with the use with فِيهِ for entering upon or carrying on a thing languidly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become languid, remiss, weak, feeble, or faint in an action or affair; to fall short in pursuing what one wants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of actions, affairs, or an object sought; the construction تَوَانَى فِي الأَمْرِ means to flag or be remiss in the affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who is languid, gentle, or grave in deportment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun applied to a woman, with the description relating to her manner of deportment.
A masculine noun; its etymological and orthographic relationship to the root is discussed separately from its meaning.
